claims.text: What the strip looks like Findings vary and can be intermittent: sinus bradycardia, non-respiratory sinus arrhythmia, SA exit block, sinus arrest (pause > 3 seconds), atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response, or bradycardia–tachycardia syndrome.
claims.quote: ECG abnormalities can be variable and intermittent. Multiple ECG abnormalities can be seen in sinus node dysfunction including: Sinus Bradycardia. Sinus Arrhythmia — associated with sinus node dysfunction in the elderly in the absence of respiratory pattern association. Sinoatrial Exit Block. Sinus Arrest — pause > 3 seconds. Atrial fibrillation with slow ventricular response. Bradycardia – tachycardia syndrome.

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Rate: slow, physiologically inappropriate
claims.quote: sinus node dysfunction causing slow, physiologically inappropriate, heart rates

claims.text: Brady–tachy variant: bradycardia alternating with paroxysmal tachycardia, often supraventricular
claims.quote: Alternating bradycardia with paroxysmal tachycardia, often supraventricular in origin.

claims.text: Rhythm: slow and irregular
claims.quote: A slow, irregular pulse suggests the diagnosis of sinus node dysfunction

claims.text: P waves (sinus arrest): no P waves for > 3 seconds
claims.quote: Prolonged absence of sinus node activity (absent P waves) > 3 seconds.

claims.text: P waves (type II SA exit block): a P wave drops out; the pause is an exact multiple of the preceding P-P interval
claims.quote: The pause surrounding the dropped P wave is an exact multiple of the preceding P-P interval.
claims.locator: Second Degree SA block, Type II

claims.text: P waves (type I SA exit block): the P-P interval shortens progressively before the dropped P wave
claims.quote: The P-P interval progressively shortens prior to the dropped P wave.
claims.locator: Second Degree SA block, Type I

claims.text: Escape beats: a pause usually triggers escape beats from a lower (atrial or junctional) pacemaker
claims.quote: The pause usually triggers escape activity in lower pacemakers (eg, atrial or junctional), preserving heart rate and function

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Mechanism: pacemaker (P) cells fail to fire → sinus pauses and arrest; transitional (T) cells fail to conduct the impulse out → SA exit block
claims.quote: Failure of the P cells to produce an impulse. This leads to sinus pauses and sinus arrest. Failure of the T cells to transmit the impulse. This leads to sino-atrial exit block.

claims.text: Intrinsic: idiopathic degenerative fibrosis (most common), ischemia, cardiomyopathies, infiltrative disease (sarcoidosis, hemochromatosis), congenital abnormalities
claims.quote: Idiopathic Degenerative Fibrosis (commonest). Ischaemia. Cardiomyopathies. Infiltrative Diseases e.g. sarcoidosis, haemochromatosis. Congenital abnormalities.

claims.text: Extrinsic: drugs (digoxin, beta blockers, calcium channel blockers), autonomic dysfunction, hypothyroidism, electrolyte abnormalities (e.g., hyperkalemia)
claims.quote: Drugs e.g. digoxin, beta-blockers, calcium channel blockers. Autonomic dysfunction. Hypothyroidism. Electrolyte abnormalitites — e.g. hyperkalaemia.

claims.text: Who: most common in the elderly, but any age can be affected
claims.quote: Commonly seen in the elderly but sinus node dysfunction can affect all age groups.

claims.text: Workup when suggested: TSH (hypothyroidism), polysomnography (sleep apnea), exercise testing (chronotropic incompetence), echocardiography (structural heart disease)
claims.quote: measurement of thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) for suspected hypothyroidism, polysomnography for suspected sleep apnea, exercise tolerance testing for suspected chronotropic incompetence, and echocardiography for suspected structural heart disease

claims.text: Symptoms Many patients are asymptomatic
claims.quote: Many patients with sick sinus syndrome are asymptomatic.

claims.text: From low cardiac output: syncope, near-syncope, dizziness, fatigue, palpitations
claims.quote: Symptoms are due to decreased cardiac output and end-organ hypoperfusion associated with cardiac rhythm abnormality. Wide range of clinical symptoms including syncope, near-syncope, dizziness, fatigue and palpitations.

claims.text: Syncope when the sinus node is slow to restart after an atrial tachyarrhythmia stops
claims.quote: Syncope may occur when the sinus node does not immediately resume function after spontaneous termination of an atrial tachyarrhythmia.

claims.text: Treatment Remove extrinsic causes (e.g., stop non-essential drugs)
claims.quote: Correction / removal of extrinsic causes e.g. non-essential drugs.

claims.text: Symptomatic with no reversible cause: pacemaker
claims.quote: Treatment of symptomatic sick sinus syndrome in the absence of an extrinsic reversible cause is pacemaker implantation

claims.text: An atrial or dual-chamber pacemaker lowers the risk of atrial fibrillation compared with a ventricular pacemaker
claims.quote: Risk of atrial fibrillation is reduced when a physiologic (atrial or atrioventricular) pacemaker rather than a ventricular pacemaker is used

claims.text: Antiarrhythmics may prevent the tachycardia runs once a pacemaker is in
claims.quote: Antiarrhythmic medications may prevent paroxysmal tachyarrhythmias after pacemaker insertion.
